title: Break The Spin · Epstein forensic
subtitle: Epstein forensic expert post. Bottom of Queue.

posts.quote: A FORENSIC EXPERT WHO STUDIED EPSTEIN'S UNRELEASED AUTOPSY FILES SAYS HE WAS LIKELY STRANGLED FROM BEHIND. NOT A SUICIDE.
posts.alt: Two panels: Jeffrey Epstein's 2013 Florida mugshot on the left and a photo of the Metropolitan Correctional Center in Manhattan, the federal jail where he died, on the right. Bold text below reads: A forensic expert who studied Epstein's unreleased autopsy files says he was likely strangled from behind. Not a suicide.
posts.caption:
"Epstein didn't kill himself" just got its most serious backing yet.

Dr. Michael Freeman, editor-in-chief of the Journal of Forensic and Legal Medicine, reviewed autopsy records, photos and files that had never been made public, provided by Epstein's brother. Working with Swedish forensic pathologist Anders Eriksson and bias researcher Itiel Dror, he presented the findings in London and told CBS News that Epstein was likely attacked and killed.

"The injuries that were documented by the medical examiner were not consistent with the suicidal hanging," Freeman said. He points to a second, lower mark on Epstein's neck: "There is no mechanism to produce a second mark that would be lower." He also describes blunt force trauma to the face and left shoulder, an injury to the back, and "what appeared to be consistent with fingernail marks above the ligature."

The team's conclusion: "The ligature marks are most consistent with homicidal strangulation from behind, most likely using a narrow knotted fabric ligature." Freeman pointed to a double-knotted orange fabric found in the cell.

New York City's medical examiner did not budge. Its office "stands by its determination" that Epstein died by suicide by hanging.
posts.first:
To be clear about what this is and is not: Freeman's analysis has not been peer-reviewed. One journal turned it down because reviewers felt criticizing a medical examiner's findings was not appropriate for peer review, and he plans to resubmit. He says he has no idea who might have killed Epstein. "All I'm interested in is, how did this get so sideways?"

A lot went sideways that night. Most of the cameras in Epstein's wing were not working. Investigators never followed up on an unexplained orange blur on a staircase leading toward his tier. None of the guards on duty spoke to medical examiner investigators, and some falsified records of their rounds. The cell was not sealed, and the body was moved within minutes.

The FBI and Justice Department concluded in 2025 that Epstein took his own life, and The New York Times reported in June that his jail notes suggested he intended to. But when the official story rests on broken cameras, missing interviews and falsified logs, Americans are right to keep asking.

Epstein's victims deserve the truth about how the man who abused them escaped trial. Let independent experts see everything and check the work.
